_openrouterNote: The day every openrouter/* row WITHOUT an `expires` date was last compared with OpenRouter's endpoints (scripts/refresh-openrouter-prices.mjs --fetch <folder> --write, answers read the same day): a row WITH a host picture is the dearest eligible host per side, raised or lowered (a row whose dearest figure depends on a price tier counts the higher of today's figure and its dearest eligible host at base price; its tier part is recorded in the row's `tiers` and not yet counted by the spend cap, and its `hosts` block says `tier_driven`), and its `hosts` block records the check date, the host count, the lowest, median and highest price and the filters used. The script refuses to move this date while a row is not on OpenRouter's list or while the answers are not from today. test/pricing-freshness.test.js turns red _openrouterStaleDays + 1 days after it: re-run the script before then (MAN-7). Direct-provider rows (anthropic/, openai/, google/...) are NOT covered by this date: they carry their own _source dates.
_asOf: Machine-readable date for the table as a whole (0.7.8): the OLDEST date every entry was last checked against its price source (its lab's page, or the OpenRouter list its _source names), so it errs old. Some entries were re-checked since (see _note and their _source); none is older. `council doctor` and `--dry-run` print it and warn past 60 days. Move it forward only when every entry has been re-checked on or after the new date. A row whose provider has retired the model or no longer lists a price (the deprecated and discontinued ones) counts as checked on the read date but keeps the figure the table already had for it, and says so in its `_source`: the date records the read, not that figure. The test (test/price-table-date.test.js) binds it to real check dates: every openrouter/ row by _openrouterCheckedAt, every direct row by the newest `read YYYY-MM-DD` in its `_source`; mock rows are not priced from a page.
_critiqueTokensNote: critiqueTokens on an entry (0.7.8) is that model's typical output for one panel review, measured from the author's own runs (reasoning models spend most of it thinking, so it runs well past the old flat 5000). Used only by the dry-run and doctor estimate, and only to RAISE a chain's estimate.critiqueTokens for that seat, never to lower it; a seat's own estimate.critiqueTokens overrides both. The spend cap does not read it: it always projects the seat's full maxTokens.
